item.text: {"text":"[TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.09784) is the closest match: BERT-style masked-item training with attention encoding absolute timestamps/positions and relative time/position differences. Its ablations support temporal attention: on Amazon Beauty, NDCG@10 falls from 0.365 to 0.352 without relative attention and to 0.347 with canonical attention; removing its auxiliary temporal contrastive loss yields 0.357. However, these ablations remove time and position components together, so they do not isolate temporal benefit against an otherwise identical position-only model. Datasets and sampled evaluation also differ from the pinned RecHarness task; reported gains are hypotheses, not transferable estimates.\n\n[TLSTSRec (online 2024; volume 2025)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) models duration and temporal spectrum with trainable timestamp matrices and adaptive long/short-term fusion. A [2026 BERT4Rec session-enhancement paper](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-026-01554-z) combines content attention with continuous time decay and gated long/short representations, but its branch and deployment changes prevent clean attribution to relative-time attention. Practical hypothesis: retain one jointly trained BERT4Rec per category and add learned, head-specific relative-time biases alongside position embeddings. Compare against the identical position-only backbone under fixed training and validation. Use observed historical timestamps only; assign the appended mask a history-derived temporal reference rather than the unknown target timestamp. Preserve masked-target training and final-nonpadding readout. Interpret recent intent and persistent affinity as latent model behavior, not observed simulator traits."}
